title: Historical V54 - Capability Reliability Kernel
summary: How SMTO records, repairs, verifies, and reports weak-model runtime failures.
html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Capability Reliability Kernel

The Reliability page shows how the operator recovered from weak-model failures: bad JSON, bad plans, wrong cwd values, command errors, Python tracebacks, failed verification, dropped final answers, and approval-envelope violations.

Smaller-model support is one reason this kernel exists. SMTO does not assume a smaller model will always plan like a larger model; it records the failure mode, applies bounded recovery, preserves approval envelopes, verifies outcomes, and turns the result into evidence that an operator can inspect.

Request fidelity is anchored by an LLM-authored immutable goal contract and an obligation-indexed evidence ledger. The runtime verifies generic coverage and effect integrity, while the LLM remains responsible for interpreting the request and choosing tools. A run is eligible for learning only after the whole-request fulfillment review accepts the evidence.

Open:

/reliability

What The Page Shows

Area Meaning
Summary Total reliability events, runs, failures, recoveries, verifications, and model profiles.
Runtime controls Reliability mode, verifier enforcement, probe budget, repair budget, weak-model action cap, and approval-envelope budget.
Models Per-model weakness and recovery counters.
Failure taxonomy Which failure classes the current model or fleet is producing most often.
Recent runs Request-level recovery timelines.
Timeline Failure detected, recovery chosen, plan compiled, envelope used, verifier result, and final outcome.
Evals Deterministic weak-model simulation runs.

Runtime Modes

Mode Behavior
aggressive Optional heavier profile. Compiles plans, records all events, and spends larger bounded recovery budgets.
standard Records and verifies with more conservative recovery defaults.
off Leaves existing operator safety in place but disables Reliability Kernel event recording and decisions.

The Agent UI's separate validation profile controls review frequency. Fast guarded skips per-action proof reviews for speed but still enforces the final whole-request fulfillment review and permits one bounded recovery attempt. Relaxed records extra review signals without blocking, while Enforced checks both each action and the final outcome. These profiles do not change the selected auto, streaming, or full_plan workflow shape.

Approval Envelopes

When a mutating plan asks for confirmation, SMTO records the approved goal, gateway, cwd values, risk ceiling, and mutation budget.

Execution repair may continue automatically only when the repaired plan stays inside that envelope. If it changes cwd, escalates risk, or uses too much mutation budget, the run pauses for confirmation again.

Reports

Select a run and use:

  • JSON for machine-readable support evidence;
  • Markdown for a customer-facing recovery report.

Reports include the timeline, failure taxonomy, recovery choices, verification status, and approval-envelope state.

Evals

Use Run in the Evals pane to execute deterministic weak-model cases. These do not require a live LLM. They cover malformed structured output, placeholders, wrong cwd, command failures, Python failures, stale verification, final-answer loss, repeated repair loops, and ambiguous stdout.

The target score for safe tasks is at least 90 percent recovered or safely blocked.

Gmail-specific reliability should follow the same pattern: preserve account scope, selected messages, preview evidence, Gmail API errors, and confirmation envelope state so a failed mail action can be explained without hiding whether anything was sent or changed.
